## Pull request overview

Updates Console’s sidebar navigation to rely on `@object-ui/layout`’s `NavigationRenderer` for search/pinning/reorder, adds a Console hook for persisted nav pins, and extends `AppSchemaRenderer` with slots so Console can inject custom sidebar content.

**Changes:**
- Console: replace custom HTML5 drag/drop + nav rendering with `NavigationRenderer` (`enableReorder`, `enablePinning`) and localStorage-backed persistence (`useNavOrder`, new `useNavPins`).
- Layout: add `sidebarHeader` and `sidebarExtra` slots to `AppSchemaRenderer` (+ tests).
- Tests/Docs: add new unit tests for slots/pins/sidebar behavior and update `ROADMAP.md`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/layout/src/AppSchemaRenderer.tsx | Adds `sidebarHeader` + `sidebarExtra` slots and wires them through `InternalSidebar`. |
| packages/layout/src/__tests__/AppSchemaRenderer.test.tsx | Adds coverage for the new slot behavior. |
| apps/console/src/hooks/useNavPins.ts | Introduces localStorage-backed navigation pin state + tree application helper. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/useNavPins.test.tsx | Adds tests for `useNavPins` persistence + pin application on nested trees. |
| apps/console/src/components/AppSidebar.tsx | Switches navigation rendering to `NavigationRenderer` and integrates reorder/pin persistence. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/AppSidebar.test.tsx | Updates tests to account for `NavigationRenderer` integration and pin/reorder wiring. |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks the navigation reorder/pin/slot work as completed. |
</details>



<details>
<summary>Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1)</summary>

**apps/console/src/components/AppSidebar.tsx:375**
* With `enablePinning` enabled, `NavigationRenderer` renders a top-level "Favorites" section for pinned navigation items. Console also renders a separate record-level "Favorites" group below, so the sidebar will show two sections with the same label, which is confusing. Consider renaming the record favorites label (e.g. "Record Favorites") or adjusting the pinned section label/rendering so the two concepts are clearly distinct.
```
         {/* Record Favorites */}
         {favorites.length > 0 && (
           <SidebarGroup>
             <SidebarGroupLabel className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
               <Star className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
```
</details>

The header comment says pinned items are shown as a "Pinned" section, but `NavigationRenderer` currently renders pinned items under a "Favorites" section. Align the doc/comment (and any user-facing wording) with the actual UI label to avoid confusion.
```suggestion
 * Pinned items are shown at the top of the sidebar in the "Favorites" section.
```

`sidebarHeader ?? (...)` prevents consumers from intentionally hiding the header by passing `null` (since `null` triggers the fallback). If you want "provided" to include `null`, switch to an `undefined` check (e.g., render the default only when `sidebarHeader === undefined`).

`NavigationRenderer`'s current `@dnd-kit` reorder implementation only wraps items in a `DndContext` when there are *no* `type: 'group'` items. In Console navigation you have grouped items (e.g. the Reports group), so `enableReorder` here will not actually render drag handles or emit `onReorder`, meaning drag reorder won't work for the common case. Either update `NavigationRenderer` to support reorder with groups/mixed content, or gate/disable `enableReorder` in Console when groups are present (and adjust expectations/tests).
```suggestion
           enableReorder={!processedNavigation.some((item: NavigationItem) => item.type === 'group')}
```

This test name claims it "persists" reorder state, but it only verifies that a pre-existing localStorage value can be loaded and that items render. Rename the test (or extend it to actually simulate a reorder and assert localStorage updates) so the intent matches the assertions.

When `MAX_PINS` is reached, `updated = [...filtered, itemId].slice(0, MAX_PINS)` drops the *newly added* pin (it keeps the oldest 20). This makes pinning appear to succeed but not actually add the item once the list is full. If the intent is to cap size while keeping the most recently pinned items, slice from the end (or explicitly drop the oldest item before appending).

`useNavPins` imports `useMemo` but never uses it, which will fail lint/TS settings that disallow unused imports. Remove `useMemo` from the import list (or use it).
```suggestion
import { useState, useCallback, useEffect } from 'react';
```
